title: Rightly Guided Caliphs and Islamic History
lines: USAT asks about the four Rightly Guided Caliphs (Khulafa ar-Rashidun), the main events of their rule, the later Muslim dynasties, and the Muslim scholars whose work shaped science and learning. Questions usually ask who did what, when, and where.
## The four caliphs at a glance
| Caliph | Rule | Title | Remembered for
| Abu Bakr (RA) | 632–634 CE (11–13 AH) | As-Siddiq | wars against false prophets and those who refused zakat; Quran gathered into one copy
| Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) | 634–644 CE (13–23 AH) | Al-Faruq | great expansion; Hijri calendar; organised government
| Uthman ibn Affan (RA) | 644–656 CE (23–35 AH) | Dhun-Nurayn | standard copies of the Quran; first Muslim navy
| Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) | 656–661 CE (35–40 AH) | Asadullah, Haidar | knowledge and justice; capital moved to Kufa
The Rashidun period lasted about 30 years. Each caliph was chosen through consultation (shura) or nomination accepted by the community, and each lived simply.
## Abu Bakr (RA)
- The Prophet's (PBUH) closest companion, first adult free man to accept Islam, and his companion in the Cave of Thawr.
- Sent the army of Usama ibn Zayd (RA), as the Prophet (PBUH) had planned.
- Fought the Wars of Apostasy (Riddah). Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA) defeated the false prophet Musaylimah at Yamamah.
- After Yamamah, had the Quran collected into one copy under Zayd ibn Thabit (RA). Nominated Umar (RA) before his death.
## Umar (RA)
- Defeated the Byzantines at Yarmuk (636 CE) and the Sasanian Persians at Qadisiyyah; Egypt was taken by Amr ibn al-As (RA).
- Jerusalem surrendered and Umar (RA) went there himself, giving its people a covenant of safety for their lives, property and churches.
- Adopted the Hijri calendar, counted from the Hijrah. Set up the diwan (registers), paid stipends, organised provinces under governors, and founded garrison cities such as Kufa, Basra and Fustat.
- Known for strict justice and accountability of officials. He was martyred while leading the dawn prayer, having named a council of six to choose his successor.
## Uthman (RA)
- Called Dhun-Nurayn, "possessor of two lights", because he married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH): Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum (RA).
- Before his caliphate, he bought the well of Rumah for the people of Madinah and funded the army for Tabuk.
- Had standard copies of the Quran prepared and sent to the provinces. Under him the first Muslim navy was formed, and expansion continued in North Africa and Persia.
- He was martyred in his house in Madinah by rebels in 656 CE.
## Ali (RA)
- Cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet (PBUH), husband of Fatimah (RA), and among the first to accept Islam as a boy.
- Famous for knowledge, eloquence, bravery (he was called Asadullah, the Lion of Allah) and fair judgement.
- Moved the capital from Madinah to Kufa. His rule faced internal conflict. He was martyred in Kufa in 661 CE.
## Later dynasties: a timeline
| Date (CE) | Event
| 661–750 | Umayyad caliphate, capital Damascus
| 711 | Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses into Spain; Gibraltar (Jabal Tariq) named after him
| 712 | Muhammad bin Qasim conquers Sindh, beginning at Debal
| 750–1258 | Abbasid caliphate; Baghdad founded as capital in 762
| 756 | Umayyad rule set up in Spain with Cordoba as capital
| 9th century | House of Wisdom (Bayt al-Hikmah) in Baghdad: translation and research
| 1187 | Salahuddin Ayyubi recaptures Jerusalem after the Battle of Hattin
| 1258 | Mongols under Hulagu sack Baghdad, ending Abbasid rule there
| 1453 | Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II conquers Constantinople
## Muslim scholars and their fields
| Scholar | Field and work
| Al-Khwarizmi | mathematics; algebra takes its name from his book; spread the Hindu-Arabic numerals
| Ibn Sina (Avicenna) | medicine and philosophy; Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb
| Al-Razi (Rhazes) | medicine; distinguished smallpox from measles
| Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen) | optics; showed that we see because light enters the eye
| Jabir ibn Hayyan | chemistry; laboratory methods
| Al-Biruni | astronomy, geography and a study of India (Kitab al-Hind)
| Al-Zahrawi | surgery; designed surgical instruments
| Ibn Khaldun | history and society; the Muqaddimah
| Ibn Battuta | travel; journeys across Africa and Asia
| Al-Idrisi | geography; a world map for Roger II of Sicily
> Which caliph adopted the Hijri calendar?  (A) Abu Bakr (RA)  (B) Umar (RA)  (C) Uthman (RA)  (D) Ali (RA)
> B. The calendar starts from the Hijrah of 622 CE but was adopted under Umar (RA), about 17 years later.
> Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb was written by  (A) Al-Biruni  (B) Ibn Khaldun  (C) Ibn Sina  (D) Al-Khwarizmi
> C. Ibn Sina's Canon of Medicine was used as a textbook in Europe for centuries.
## Traps
! Gathering the Quran into one copy was under Abu Bakr (RA); standard copies were under Uthman (RA).
! Damascus was the Umayyad capital; Baghdad the Abbasid capital; Cordoba the capital in Spain.
! Muhammad bin Qasim (712) is linked with Sindh; Tariq ibn Ziyad (711) with Spain.
## Quick check
- Order: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali (RA); about 30 years in all.
- Umar (RA): Hijri calendar, diwan, Jerusalem. Uthman (RA): standard Quran, navy. Ali (RA): Kufa.
- Umayyads Damascus 661; Abbasids Baghdad 750; Baghdad falls 1258; Constantinople 1453.
